answer: Like layers of shale, an agent economy can gate entry through social-graph distance: a newcomer may only trade after an established agent within two hops vouches for it, and each voucher holds a small, slowly refilling quota of introductions. A thousand fake identities mean nothing without real introductions, and buying them is costly, because one bad vouch burns the introducer's own reputation and quota. An umber stain of past fraud follows the voucher on-chain, and each introduction is sealed with a cipher signature so it cannot be faked or replayed.
